# Control reference

<!-- Generated by tools/Export-ControlDocs.ps1 from the catalog in src/WindowsServerHardening/Controls. Do not edit by hand. -->

Windows Server Hardening Toolkit v2.0.0 ships **107 controls** in 10 categories.

Legend: **Opt-in** controls run only when a profile lists them in `EnableControls` (or when selected with `-ControlId`). **Audit-only** controls are evaluated but never changed automatically. **Restart** marks settings that take effect after a reboot. **From** marks controls that are reported as not applicable on older Windows Server releases where the feature does not exist.

Benchmark references quote the CIS recommendation title rather than its number, because numbering changes between benchmark versions. Always validate against the benchmark version your organisation has adopted.

## SMB

| ID | Severity | Control | Expected | Method | ATT&CK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMB-001 | Critical | SMBv1 server protocol is disabled | False | SMB server: `EnableSMB1Protocol` | [T1210](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/) |  |
| SMB-002 | High | SMBv1 client driver is disabled | 4 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\mrxsmb10\Start` | [T1210](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/) | Restart |
| SMB-003 | High | SMB server requires packet signing | True | SMB server: `RequireSecuritySignature` | [T1557.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/001/) |  |
| SMB-004 | High | SMB client requires packet signing | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters\RequireSecuritySignature` | [T1557.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/001/) |  |
| SMB-005 | Medium | SMB server encrypts data in transit | True | SMB server: `EncryptData` | [T1040](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1040/) [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) |  |
| SMB-006 | High | Anonymous access to named pipes and shares is restricted | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters\RestrictNullSessAccess` | [T1135](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1135/) [T1087](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/) |  |
| SMB-007 | Medium | Insecure guest logons to SMB servers are disabled | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\LanmanWorkstation\AllowInsecureGuestAuth` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) | From: Windows Server 2016 |

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **SMB-001 SMBv1 server protocol is disabled**: SMBv1 lacks pre-authentication integrity and encryption and was the attack surface for EternalBlue (MS17-010), used by WannaCry and NotPetya. *Impact:* Clients that only speak SMBv1 (Windows XP / Server 2003, old NAS and printers) can no longer connect to this server. *Benchmark:* CIS: Configure SMB v1 server = Disabled.
- **SMB-002 SMBv1 client driver is disabled**: The SMBv1 client driver lets this server connect to legacy SMBv1 shares and exposes it to the same protocol weaknesses as the SMBv1 server. *Impact:* The server can no longer access file shares that only support SMBv1. *Benchmark:* CIS: Configure SMB v1 client driver = Enabled: Disable driver.
- **SMB-003 SMB server requires packet signing**: Without mandatory signing, captured NTLM authentications can be relayed to this server (SMB relay) and SMB traffic can be tampered with in transit. *Impact:* Small throughput cost on very high-volume file servers; all supported Windows clients support signing. *Benchmark:* CIS: Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always) = Enabled.
- **SMB-004 SMB client requires packet signing**: Requiring signing on outbound SMB sessions prevents attackers from impersonating file servers or modifying data this server reads, such as scripts on SYSVOL. *Impact:* The server cannot connect to SMB servers that do not support signing. *Benchmark:* CIS: Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always) = Enabled.
- **SMB-005 SMB server encrypts data in transit**: SMB 3 encryption protects file contents and credentials-derived data on the wire against sniffing on untrusted network segments. *Impact:* Clients that do not support SMB 3.0 (Windows 7 / Server 2008 R2 and older) are refused access. Exclude this control if such clients must connect. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: SMB security enhancements (SMB encryption).
- **SMB-006 Anonymous access to named pipes and shares is restricted**: Null sessions let unauthenticated users enumerate shares and pipes and gather reconnaissance information about the server and domain. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares = Enabled.
- **SMB-007 Insecure guest logons to SMB servers are disabled**: Guest (unauthenticated) SMB access disables signing and encryption and makes the server trust rogue file servers. *Benchmark:* CIS: Enable insecure guest logons = Disabled.

</details>

## Authentication

| ID | Severity | Control | Expected | Method | ATT&CK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AUTH-001 | Critical | LAN Manager authentication level is NTLMv2 only | 5 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\LmCompatibilityLevel` | [T1557.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/001/) [T1550.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1550/002/) [T1110.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/002/) |  |
| AUTH-002 | High | LAN Manager password hashes are not stored | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\NoLMHash` | [T1003.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/002/) [T1110.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/002/) |  |
| AUTH-003 | Critical | WDigest does not cache cleartext credentials | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential` | [T1003.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/) |  |
| AUTH-004 | High | LSASS runs as a protected process (RunAsPPL) | One of: 1, 2 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPL` | [T1003.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/) | Restart, From: Windows Server 2012 R2 |
| AUTH-005 | Medium | NTLM SSP server sessions require NTLMv2 and 128-bit encryption | 537395200 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0\NTLMMinServerSec` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) |  |
| AUTH-006 | Medium | NTLM SSP client sessions require NTLMv2 and 128-bit encryption | 537395200 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0\NTLMMinClientSec` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) |  |
| AUTH-007 | High | Local accounts with blank passwords are limited to console logon | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\LimitBlankPasswordUse` | [T1078.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/003/) |  |
| AUTH-008 | High | CredSSP encryption oracle remediation is set to Force Updated Clients | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\CredSSP\Parameters\AllowEncryptionOracle` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) [T1210](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/) |  |
| AUTH-009 | Medium | Anonymous SID/name translation is disabled | 0 | Security policy: `LSAAnonymousNameLookup` | [T1087](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/) |  |
| AUTH-010 | High | Anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts is not allowed | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RestrictAnonymousSAM` | [T1087.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/001/) [T1087.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/002/) [T1110.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/) |  |
| AUTH-011 | High | Anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares is not allowed | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RestrictAnonymous` | [T1087](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/) [T1135](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1135/) |  |
| AUTH-012 | Medium | Everyone permissions do not apply to anonymous users | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\EveryoneIncludesAnonymous` | [T1135](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1135/) |  |
| AUTH-013 | High | Credential Guard is running | Running | Check: CredentialGuard | [T1003.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/) [T1550.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1550/002/) [T1558](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1558/) | Audit-only, Not on: DomainController, From: Windows Server 2016 |

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **AUTH-001 LAN Manager authentication level is NTLMv2 only**: Levels below 5 accept LM and NTLMv1 responses, which can be cracked or downgraded and relayed in minutes. *Impact:* Legacy systems and appliances that only support LM/NTLMv1 can no longer authenticate. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network security: LAN Manager authentication level = Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM.
- **AUTH-002 LAN Manager password hashes are not stored**: LM hashes are trivially reversible; storing them in the SAM gives an attacker with SAM access the cleartext passwords. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change = Enabled.
- **AUTH-003 WDigest does not cache cleartext credentials**: When enabled, WDigest keeps plaintext passwords in LSASS memory where tools such as Mimikatz can read them. It is off by default from Windows Server 2012 R2; on Windows Server 2012 it must be disabled explicitly (KB2871997). *Benchmark:* CIS: WDigest Authentication = Disabled.
- **AUTH-004 LSASS runs as a protected process (RunAsPPL)**: LSA protection blocks non-protected processes, including most credential dumping tools, from reading LSASS memory or injecting code into it. Value 1 enables it with a UEFI lock, value 2 (Windows 11 22H2 / Server 2025 and later) without. *Impact:* Third-party LSA plug-ins and smart card drivers that are not signed for protected processes stop loading. Test with the CodeIntegrity event log first. *Benchmark:* CIS: Configure LSASS to run as a protected process = Enabled.
- **AUTH-005 NTLM SSP server sessions require NTLMv2 and 128-bit encryption**: Requiring NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption prevents downgrade to weak NTLM session keys. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) servers = Require NTLMv2 session security, Require 128-bit encryption.
- **AUTH-006 NTLM SSP client sessions require NTLMv2 and 128-bit encryption**: Ensures outbound NTLM sessions from this server cannot be negotiated down to weak session security. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients = Require NTLMv2 session security, Require 128-bit encryption.
- **AUTH-007 Local accounts with blank passwords are limited to console logon**: Prevents network logons (SMB, RDP, WinRM) with local accounts that have an empty password. *Benchmark:* CIS: Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only = Enabled.
- **AUTH-008 CredSSP encryption oracle remediation is set to Force Updated Clients**: Mitigates CVE-2018-0886, a CredSSP flaw that allows remote code execution through a man-in-the-middle position during RDP or WinRM authentication. *Impact:* Unpatched RDP clients or servers can no longer establish CredSSP sessions with this server. *Benchmark:* CIS: Encryption Oracle Remediation = Enabled: Force Updated Clients.
- **AUTH-009 Anonymous SID/name translation is disabled**: Anonymous SID-to-name lookups allow unauthenticated users to resolve the built-in Administrator account name even when it was renamed. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation = Disabled.
- **AUTH-010 Anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts is not allowed**: Blocks unauthenticated users from listing local and domain accounts, a common first step in password spraying. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts = Enabled.
- **AUTH-011 Anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares is not allowed**: Prevents anonymous users from enumerating account names and network shares. *Impact:* Very old applications that rely on anonymous enumeration (for example NT4-era trusts) stop working. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares = Enabled.
- **AUTH-012 Everyone permissions do not apply to anonymous users**: Keeps anonymous users from inheriting access granted to the Everyone group on files, shares and registry keys. *Benchmark:* CIS: Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users = Disabled.
- **AUTH-013 Credential Guard is running**: Credential Guard isolates NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets in a virtualization-based enclave so they cannot be dumped from LSASS, even by an administrator. *Impact:* Not supported on domain controllers; breaks NTLMv1, MS-CHAPv2 and unconstrained Kerberos delegation on the protected host. *Benchmark:* CIS: Turn On Virtualization Based Security: Credential Guard Configuration = Enabled with UEFI lock.

</details>

## AccountPolicy

| ID | Severity | Control | Expected | Method | ATT&CK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACCT-001 | High | Minimum password length | >= 14 | Security policy: `MinimumPasswordLength` | [T1110](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/) [T1110.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/002/) | Parameter `MinimumPasswordLength` |
| ACCT-002 | Medium | Password history size | >= 24 | Security policy: `PasswordHistorySize` | [T1110](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/) | Parameter `PasswordHistorySize` |
| ACCT-003 | Medium | Maximum password age | Between 1 and 365 | Security policy: `MaximumPasswordAge` | [T1078](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/) | Parameter `MaximumPasswordAge` |
| ACCT-004 | Low | Minimum password age | >= 1 | Security policy: `MinimumPasswordAge` | [T1110](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/) | Parameter `MinimumPasswordAge` |
| ACCT-005 | High | Passwords must meet complexity requirements | 1 | Security policy: `PasswordComplexity` | [T1110.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/001/) [T1110.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/) |  |
| ACCT-006 | High | Passwords are not stored using reversible encryption | 0 | Security policy: `ClearTextPassword` | [T1003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/) |  |
| ACCT-007 | High | Account lockout threshold | Between 1 and 5 | Security policy: `LockoutBadCount` | [T1110.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/001/) [T1110.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/) | Parameter `LockoutThreshold` |
| ACCT-008 | Medium | Account lockout duration | >= 15 | Security policy: `LockoutDuration` | [T1110](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/) | Parameter `LockoutDuration` |
| ACCT-009 | Medium | Reset account lockout counter after | >= 15 | Security policy: `ResetLockoutCount` | [T1110.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/) | Parameter `ResetLockoutCount` |
| ACCT-010 | High | Built-in Guest account is disabled | 0 | Security policy: `EnableGuestAccount` | [T1078.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/001/) |  |

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **ACCT-001 Minimum password length**: Password length is the strongest single factor against offline cracking and guessing attacks. *Impact:* Applies at the next password change of local accounts. On domain members, domain password policy applies to domain accounts. *Benchmark:* CIS: Minimum password length = 14 or more character(s).
- **ACCT-002 Password history size**: Stops users from cycling back to previously compromised passwords. *Benchmark:* CIS: Enforce password history = 24 or more password(s).
- **ACCT-003 Maximum password age**: Passwords that never expire (value -1 or 0) remain valid indefinitely after a silent compromise. *Benchmark:* CIS: Maximum password age = 365 or fewer days, but not 0.
- **ACCT-004 Minimum password age**: Without a minimum age, users can immediately cycle through the password history and reuse their old password. *Benchmark:* CIS: Minimum password age = 1 or more day(s).
- **ACCT-005 Passwords must meet complexity requirements**: Complexity rules prevent dictionary words and account names from being used as passwords. *Benchmark:* CIS: Password must meet complexity requirements = Enabled.
- **ACCT-006 Passwords are not stored using reversible encryption**: Reversible encryption is equivalent to storing passwords in cleartext. *Benchmark:* CIS: Store passwords using reversible encryption = Disabled.
- **ACCT-007 Account lockout threshold**: A threshold of 0 never locks accounts, allowing unlimited online password guessing. *Impact:* Accounts lock after repeated failures, which can be abused for denial of service against known account names. *Benchmark:* CIS: Account lockout threshold = 5 or fewer invalid logon attempt(s), but not 0.
- **ACCT-008 Account lockout duration**: A sufficient lockout duration slows down brute-force attacks to an impractical rate. *Benchmark:* CIS: Account lockout duration = 15 or more minute(s).
- **ACCT-009 Reset account lockout counter after**: A short observation window lets attackers spread guesses just below the lockout threshold. *Impact:* Must be less than or equal to the lockout duration, otherwise secedit rejects the policy. *Benchmark:* CIS: Reset account lockout counter after = 15 or more minute(s).
- **ACCT-010 Built-in Guest account is disabled**: The Guest account allows unauthenticated access to the server and its shares. *Benchmark:* CIS: Accounts: Guest account status = Disabled.

</details>

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **LOG-001 Advanced audit policy overrides legacy category settings**: Without this setting, legacy category-level audit policy can silently overwrite the granular subcategory configuration below. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings to override audit policy category settings = Enabled.
- **LOG-002 Audit Credential Validation**: Records NTLM credential validation (events 4776), the primary signal for password spraying and brute-force attempts. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Credential Validation = Success and Failure.
- **LOG-003 Audit Kerberos Authentication Service**: TGT requests (event 4768/4771) reveal AS-REP roasting, password spraying and unusual encryption types on domain controllers. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Kerberos Authentication Service = Success and Failure (DC only).
- **LOG-004 Audit Kerberos Service Ticket Operations**: Service ticket requests (event 4769) are needed to detect Kerberoasting. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Kerberos Service Ticket Operations = Success and Failure (DC only).
- **LOG-005 Audit Security Group Management**: Records membership changes of security groups such as local Administrators or Domain Admins. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Security Group Management = include Success.
- **LOG-006 Audit User Account Management**: Records account creation, deletion, password resets and enabling of accounts, which attackers use for persistence. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit User Account Management = Success and Failure.
- **LOG-007 Audit Process Creation**: Process creation events (4688) are the foundation of endpoint detection for malicious execution. *Impact:* Increases Security log volume; size the log accordingly (see LOG-018). *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Process Creation = include Success.
- **LOG-008 Audit Account Lockout**: Lockout events (4625 with lockout status) help correlate brute-force activity. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Account Lockout = include Failure.
- **LOG-009 Audit Logoff**: Logoff events complete session timelines during incident investigations. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Logoff = include Success.
- **LOG-010 Audit Logon**: Successful and failed logons (4624/4625) are essential for detecting lateral movement and credential abuse. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Logon = Success and Failure.
- **LOG-011 Audit Special Logon**: Event 4672 flags logons that receive administrative privileges. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Special Logon = include Success.
- **LOG-012 Audit Removable Storage**: Records file access on removable media for data exfiltration and malware introduction investigations. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Removable Storage = Success and Failure.
- **LOG-013 Audit Audit Policy Change**: Detects attackers disabling auditing to cover their tracks. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Audit Policy Change = include Success.
- **LOG-014 Audit Authentication Policy Change**: Records changes to trusts, Kerberos policy and user rights that weaken authentication. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Authentication Policy Change = include Success.
- **LOG-015 Audit Sensitive Privilege Use**: Records use of privileges such as SeDebugPrivilege and SeTcbPrivilege that credential theft tools require. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Sensitive Privilege Use = Success and Failure.
- **LOG-016 Audit Security System Extension**: Records loading of authentication packages and service installation (event 4697), common persistence techniques. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit Security System Extension = include Success.
- **LOG-017 Audit System Integrity**: Records violations of the security subsystem integrity, including audit log tampering and code integrity failures. *Benchmark:* CIS: Audit System Integrity = Success and Failure.
- **LOG-018 Security event log maximum size**: A small Security log rolls over quickly and loses the evidence needed to investigate an incident. *Benchmark:* CIS: Security: Specify the maximum log file size (KB) = 196,608 or greater.
- **LOG-019 Application event log maximum size**: Keeps enough application history for troubleshooting and investigation. *Benchmark:* CIS: Application: Specify the maximum log file size (KB) = 32,768 or greater.
- **LOG-020 System event log maximum size**: Keeps enough service and driver history, including service installation events (7045). *Benchmark:* CIS: System: Specify the maximum log file size (KB) = 32,768 or greater.
- **LOG-021 Command line is included in process creation events**: Command lines turn process creation events into actionable detections (encoded PowerShell, LOLBins, ransomware tooling). *Impact:* Command lines can contain secrets passed as arguments; restrict who can read the Security log. *Benchmark:* CIS: Include command line in process creation events = Enabled.
- **LOG-022 PowerShell script block logging is enabled**: Logs the de-obfuscated content of executed PowerShell (event 4104), defeating most encoding tricks used by attackers. *Impact:* Increases the size of the PowerShell Operational log. *Benchmark:* CIS: Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging = Enabled.

</details>

## Firewall

| ID | Severity | Control | Expected | Method | ATT&CK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FW-001 | Critical | Windows Firewall is enabled on all profiles | True | Firewall profile: `Enabled` | [T1562.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/004/) [T1021](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/) |  |
| FW-002 | High | Inbound connections are blocked by default on all profiles | Block | Firewall profile: `DefaultInboundAction` | [T1562.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/004/) [T1021](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/) |  |
| FW-003 | Low | Firewall logs dropped packets on all profiles | True | Firewall profile: `LogBlocked` | [T1046](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/) |  |
| FW-004 | Low | Firewall log size is at least 16 MB on all profiles | >= 16384 | Firewall profile: `LogMaxSizeKilobytes` | [T1046](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/) | Parameter `FirewallLogMaxSizeKB` |
| FW-005 | Medium | Inbound Telnet (TCP 23) is explicitly blocked | Present | Firewall rule: `WSH-Block-Telnet-In` | [T1021](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/) [T1040](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1040/) |  |
| FW-006 | Low | Inbound FTP (TCP 21) is explicitly blocked | Present | Firewall rule: `WSH-Block-FTP-In` | [T1040](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1040/) [T1105](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/) |  |
| FW-007 | High | Remote Desktop is not reachable from any address | 0 | Check: RdpFirewallScope | [T1021.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/) [T1133](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1133/) [T1110](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/) | Audit-only |

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **FW-001 Windows Firewall is enabled on all profiles**: The host firewall is the last line of defence against lateral movement and exposure of management services. *Benchmark:* CIS: Windows Firewall: <Domain\|Private\|Public>: Firewall state = On.
- **FW-002 Inbound connections are blocked by default on all profiles**: A default-deny inbound posture ensures only explicitly allowed services are reachable. *Impact:* Services without an allow rule become unreachable. Built-in Windows roles create their own rules. *Benchmark:* CIS: Windows Firewall: <Domain\|Private\|Public>: Inbound connections = Block (default).
- **FW-003 Firewall logs dropped packets on all profiles**: Dropped packet logs reveal scanning and blocked lateral movement attempts. *Benchmark:* CIS: Windows Firewall: <Domain\|Private\|Public>: Logging: Log dropped packets = Yes.
- **FW-004 Firewall log size is at least 16 MB on all profiles**: The default 4 MB firewall log overwrites itself within minutes on a busy server. *Benchmark:* CIS: Windows Firewall: <Domain\|Private\|Public>: Logging: Size limit (KB) = 16,384 KB or greater.
- **FW-005 Inbound Telnet (TCP 23) is explicitly blocked**: Telnet transmits credentials in cleartext. An explicit block rule takes precedence over any allow rule added later. *Benchmark:* Hardening best practice: block cleartext management protocols.
- **FW-006 Inbound FTP (TCP 21) is explicitly blocked**: FTP transmits credentials and data in cleartext; use SFTP or FTPS instead. *Impact:* Breaks FTP services hosted on this server. The WebServer profile excludes this control. *Benchmark:* Hardening best practice: block cleartext file transfer protocols.
- **FW-007 Remote Desktop is not reachable from any address**: RDP exposed to every address is a leading initial access vector for ransomware operators. *Benchmark:* Hardening best practice: restrict management protocols to administrative networks.

</details>

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **SVC-001 Print Spooler service is disabled**: The Print Spooler has a long history of critical vulnerabilities (PrintNightmare CVE-2021-34527) and enables coercion attacks such as PrinterBug. *Impact:* The server can no longer share or print. Exclude this control on print servers and servers that need to print. *Benchmark:* CIS: Print Spooler (Spooler) = Disabled (required on domain controllers).
- **SVC-002 Remote Registry service is disabled**: Remote Registry lets remote users read and modify the registry, which is used for reconnaissance and lateral movement. *Impact:* Some legacy monitoring and inventory tools that read the registry remotely stop working. *Benchmark:* CIS: Remote Registry (RemoteRegistry) = Disabled.
- **SVC-003 Telnet server is disabled**: Telnet provides remote shell access with cleartext credentials. *Benchmark:* Hardening best practice: remove cleartext remote shells.
- **SVC-004 SNMP service is disabled**: SNMP v1/v2c uses cleartext community strings and leaks detailed system and network information. *Impact:* Monitoring systems that poll SNMP stop receiving data; prefer WMI/WinRM or SNMPv3 agents. *Benchmark:* CIS: SNMP Service (SNMP) = Disabled or Not Installed.
- **SVC-005 Simple TCP/IP Services are disabled**: Echo, discard, chargen and similar legacy services have no business use and can be abused for amplification. *Benchmark:* CIS: Simple TCP/IP Services (simptcp) = Disabled or Not Installed.
- **SVC-006 Remote Access Auto Connection Manager is disabled**: Automatically dialing remote networks is not required on servers and increases attack surface. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.
- **SVC-007 SSDP Discovery service is disabled**: SSDP/UPnP discovery is a consumer feature that exposes the host to network discovery and UPnP attacks. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.
- **SVC-008 UPnP Device Host service is disabled**: Hosting UPnP devices is not a server workload and adds unauthenticated network attack surface. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.
- **SVC-009 Xbox Live Auth Manager service is disabled**: Consumer gaming services have no place on a server and only add attack surface. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.
- **SVC-010 Xbox Live Game Save service is disabled**: Consumer gaming services have no place on a server and only add attack surface. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.
- **SVC-011 Geolocation service is disabled**: Location tracking is not needed on servers. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.
- **SVC-012 Downloaded Maps Manager service is disabled**: Offline maps are a client feature that is not needed on servers. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.
- **SVC-013 Windows Mobile Hotspot service is disabled**: A mobile hotspot could bridge the server network to an uncontrolled wireless network. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.
- **SVC-014 Remote Procedure Call Locator is disabled**: The legacy RPC name service is only needed by very old applications. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: disabling system services on Windows Server with Desktop Experience.

</details>

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **SYS-001 User Account Control is enabled (Admin Approval Mode)**: With UAC disabled every administrator process runs with a full token, removing a key barrier against malware. *Benchmark:* CIS: User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode = Enabled.
- **SYS-002 Admin Approval Mode applies to the built-in Administrator**: Without this, the built-in Administrator account always runs elevated and bypasses UAC entirely. *Impact:* The built-in Administrator receives elevation prompts like other administrators. *Benchmark:* CIS: User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account = Enabled.
- **SYS-003 Elevation prompt for administrators uses the secure desktop**: Prompting on the secure desktop prevents other processes from spoofing or auto-approving the elevation dialog. *Benchmark:* CIS: User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode = Prompt for consent on the secure desktop.
- **SYS-004 UAC restrictions apply to local accounts on network logons**: Filtering the token of local administrators on network logons blocks pass-the-hash with local Administrator accounts. *Impact:* Remote administration with local (non-domain) administrator accounts no longer receives full rights; use domain accounts or LAPS. *Benchmark:* CIS: Apply UAC restrictions to local accounts on network logons = Enabled (member servers).
- **SYS-005 AutoPlay is turned off for all drives**: AutoPlay can launch content from removable or network media without user intent. *Benchmark:* CIS: Turn off Autoplay = Enabled: All drives.
- **SYS-006 AutoRun commands are not executed**: Blocks autorun.inf commands, a classic malware propagation method through USB devices. *Benchmark:* CIS: Set the default behavior for AutoRun = Enabled: Do not execute any autorun commands.
- **SYS-007 Last signed-in user name is not displayed**: Showing the last user name on the logon screen discloses valid (often administrative) account names. *Benchmark:* CIS: Interactive logon: Do not display last signed-in = Enabled.
- **SYS-008 Machine inactivity limit locks idle sessions**: Unattended unlocked console and RDP sessions give anyone with physical or session access full control. *Benchmark:* CIS: Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit = 900 or fewer second(s), but not 0.
- **SYS-009 Logon banner title is configured**: A legal notice establishes that access is monitored and supports prosecution of unauthorized use. *Benchmark:* CIS: Interactive logon: Message title for users attempting to log on = configured.
- **SYS-010 Logon banner text is configured**: A legal notice establishes that access is monitored and supports prosecution of unauthorized use. *Benchmark:* CIS: Interactive logon: Message text for users attempting to log on = configured.
- **SYS-011 Structured Exception Handling Overwrite Protection (SEHOP) is enabled**: SEHOP blocks a widely used class of stack-based exploitation techniques. *Benchmark:* CIS: Enable Structured Exception Handling Overwrite Protection (SEHOP) = Enabled.
- **SYS-012 Data Execution Prevention covers all processes**: DEP in OptOut or AlwaysOn mode prevents code execution from data pages for every process, not only for Windows components. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: Data Execution Prevention.
- **SYS-013 UEFI Secure Boot is enabled**: Secure Boot ensures only signed boot loaders run, protecting against bootkits, and is a prerequisite for Credential Guard. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: Secure the Windows boot process.
- **SYS-014 Windows Script Host is disabled**: Blocks VBScript and JScript droppers executed through wscript.exe and cscript.exe. *Impact:* Opt-in: breaks VBScript logon scripts, some installers and management agents that rely on WSH. Enable via the profile EnableControls list after testing. *Benchmark:* Hardening best practice: disable unused script interpreters.

</details>

| ID | Severity | Control | Expected | Method | ATT&CK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RDP-001 | High | Network Level Authentication is required for RDP | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\UserAuthentication` | [T1021.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/) [T1210](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/) |  |
| RDP-002 | Medium | RDP security layer is TLS | 2 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\SecurityLayer` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) |  |
| RDP-003 | Medium | RDP client connection encryption level is High | 3 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\MinEncryptionLevel` | [T1040](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1040/) |  |
| RDP-004 | Medium | RDP always prompts for a password | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\fPromptForPassword` | [T1021.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/) [T1078](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/) |  |
| RDP-005 | Medium | RDP clients cannot save passwords | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\DisablePasswordSaving` | [T1555.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/004/) |  |
| RDP-006 | Medium | RDP drive redirection is disabled | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\fDisableCdm` | [T1105](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/) [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/) |  |
| RDP-007 | Low | RDP clipboard redirection is disabled | 1 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\fDisableClip` | [T1115](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1115/) | Opt-in |

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **RDP-001 Network Level Authentication is required for RDP**: NLA authenticates users before a full RDP session is created, shielding the server from pre-authentication exploits such as BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708) and resource exhaustion. *Benchmark:* CIS: Require user authentication for remote connections by using Network Level Authentication = Enabled.
- **RDP-002 RDP security layer is TLS**: The native RDP security layer does not authenticate the server, allowing man-in-the-middle interception. *Benchmark:* CIS: Require use of specific security layer for remote (RDP) connections = SSL.
- **RDP-003 RDP client connection encryption level is High**: Requires 128-bit encryption for RDP sessions that do not use TLS. *Benchmark:* CIS: Set client connection encryption level = High Level.
- **RDP-004 RDP always prompts for a password**: Prevents RDP connections that reuse credentials stored in an attacker-controlled .rdp file or client. *Benchmark:* CIS: Always prompt for password upon connection = Enabled.
- **RDP-005 RDP clients cannot save passwords**: Saved RDP credentials in Credential Manager are a common target for credential harvesting. *Benchmark:* CIS: Do not allow passwords to be saved = Enabled.
- **RDP-006 RDP drive redirection is disabled**: Mapped client drives provide an easy path to copy tools onto the server and exfiltrate data. *Impact:* Administrators can no longer copy files through mapped drives in RDP sessions. *Benchmark:* CIS: Do not allow drive redirection = Enabled.
- **RDP-007 RDP clipboard redirection is disabled**: Clipboard redirection can leak data out of, or move payloads into, the server. *Impact:* Opt-in: copy and paste between the admin workstation and the server stops working. *Benchmark:* CIS (Level 2): Do not allow Clipboard redirection = Enabled.

</details>

| NET-005 | High | SSL 2.0 is disabled for server connections | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\SSL 2.0\Server\Enabled` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) [T1040](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1040/) | Restart |
| NET-006 | High | SSL 3.0 is disabled for server connections | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\SSL 3.0\Server\Enabled` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) [T1040](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1040/) | Restart |
| NET-007 | Medium | TLS 1.0 is disabled for server connections | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.0\Server\Enabled` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) [T1040](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1040/) | Opt-in, Restart |
| NET-008 | Medium | TLS 1.1 is disabled for server connections | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.1\Server\Enabled` | [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) [T1040](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1040/) | Opt-in, Restart |

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **NET-001 LLMNR (multicast name resolution) is disabled**: LLMNR responses can be spoofed by any host on the subnet to capture NTLM hashes (Responder-style attacks). *Benchmark:* CIS: Turn off multicast name resolution = Enabled.
- **NET-002 NetBIOS name resolution uses P-node (no broadcasts)**: P-node stops NetBIOS broadcast name queries, which are poisoned in the same way as LLMNR. *Impact:* NetBIOS names are then resolved only through WINS; environments that rely on broadcast resolution must use DNS. *Benchmark:* CIS: NetBT NodeType configuration = P-node.
- **NET-003 IP source routing is disabled**: Source-routed packets let an attacker dictate the network path and bypass filtering. *Benchmark:* CIS: MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting) IP source routing protection level = Highest protection, source routing is completely disabled.
- **NET-004 ICMP redirects cannot override routes**: Forged ICMP redirects can reroute server traffic through an attacker-controlled host. *Benchmark:* CIS: MSS: (EnableICMPRedirect) Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes = Disabled.
- **NET-005 SSL 2.0 is disabled for server connections**: SSL 2.0 is fundamentally broken and must never be negotiated. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: TLS/SSL settings (SCHANNEL protocols).
- **NET-006 SSL 3.0 is disabled for server connections**: SSL 3.0 is vulnerable to POODLE and must not be offered by servers. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: TLS/SSL settings (SCHANNEL protocols).
- **NET-007 TLS 1.0 is disabled for server connections**: TLS 1.0 relies on deprecated cryptography and is no longer accepted by PCI DSS and most compliance frameworks. *Impact:* Opt-in: older clients, SQL Server versions and .NET applications without TLS 1.2 support lose connectivity. Enabled by the WebServer profile. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: TLS/SSL settings (SCHANNEL protocols).
- **NET-008 TLS 1.1 is disabled for server connections**: TLS 1.1 is deprecated (RFC 8996) and should be replaced by TLS 1.2 or 1.3. *Impact:* Opt-in: clients limited to TLS 1.1 lose connectivity. Enabled by the WebServer profile. *Benchmark:* Microsoft guidance: TLS/SSL settings (SCHANNEL protocols).

</details>

## WindowsUpdate

| ID | Severity | Control | Expected | Method | ATT&CK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WU-001 | High | Automatic Updates are enabled by policy | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU\NoAutoUpdate` | [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/) [T1210](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/) |  |
| WU-002 | Medium | Updates are downloaded automatically and installed on a schedule | 4 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU\AUOptions` | [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/) |  |
| WU-003 | Low | Scheduled install day is configured | 0 | Registry: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU\ScheduledInstallDay` |  | Parameter `ScheduledInstallDay` |
| WU-004 | High | Security updates were installed recently | <= 35 | Check: UpdateRecency | [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/) [T1210](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/) [T1068](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/) | Audit-only, Parameter `MaxDaysSinceLastUpdate` |
| WU-005 | High | No software updates are pending installation | 0 | Check: PendingUpdates | [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/) [T1210](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/) | Audit-only |

<details><summary>Rationale and impact</summary>

- **WU-001 Automatic Updates are enabled by policy**: Unpatched servers are the most common root cause of successful intrusions. *Impact:* If updates are managed by WSUS, SCCM or Azure Update Manager, exclude the WU controls or align them with that tooling. *Benchmark:* CIS: Configure Automatic Updates = Enabled.
- **WU-002 Updates are downloaded automatically and installed on a schedule**: Option 4 (auto download and schedule the install) ensures patches are applied without depending on manual action. *Impact:* The server installs updates and may restart at the scheduled time (see WU-003). *Benchmark:* CIS: Configure Automatic Updates = 4 - Auto download and schedule the install.
- **WU-003 Scheduled install day is configured**: A defined install day (0 = every day) keeps the patch window predictable and short. *Benchmark:* CIS: Configure Automatic Updates: Scheduled install day = 0 - Every day.
- **WU-004 Security updates were installed recently**: Microsoft ships cumulative security updates monthly; a server without an update in more than about a month is missing security fixes. *Benchmark:* Patch management best practice.
- **WU-005 No software updates are pending installation**: Approved but uninstalled updates leave known vulnerabilities open. *Impact:* The scan queries Windows Update or WSUS and can take several minutes. Set the profile parameter SkipPendingUpdateScan to true to skip it. *Benchmark:* Patch management best practice.

</details>
